outOfScope: Moving product/domain scheduling, acceptance, publication or recovery authority into Oracle.
Treating historical BB-060..064 READY/Jev artifacts as current implementation authority.
Claiming live coding-agent or product value from deterministic research prototypes or source inspection.
constraints: Research must inspect current source plus primary external evidence, distinguish retained findings from superseded assumptions, and compare reuse with the smallest ExHarness-owned seam.
Application/domain authority remains outside Oracle; Core consumes semantic context but does not own provider/source-specific retrieval.
Required context is budgeted, provenance-bound and currentness-checked; missing or ambiguous required evidence fails closed.
Worker execution is unauthorized until researchGaps are empty and a new exact Jev readiness judgment is SATISFIED.
invariants: Application/domain controllers own work semantics, acceptance, publication, recovery and product authority; Oracle only resolves context.
Every ContextResolution is bounded by explicit requirement/budget and preserves source provenance/currentness; missing or ambiguous required evidence fails closed.
Oracle is infrastructure-owned and provider/planner internals do not become model-visible scheduling authority or Core/Application implementation ownership.
architectureDecisions: ContextRequirement is caller-facing and provider-neutral: semantic need, required/optional evidence, currentness constraints, consumer identity and budget.
ContextResolution is durable evidence: requirement identity, source/currentness identities, materialization identity, provenance, budget consumed, resolved items and explicit missing/partial state.
Current Backend repository and QA accepted-artifact flows are compatibility examples, not separate final APIs.
Provider-specific queries and planning stay below the semantic contract; a ContextRequirement cannot grant scheduling, acceptance, publication or recovery authority.
implementationSlices: Derive the semantic fields and identity rules from current Backend/QA flows plus runtime needs.
Implement a deterministic contract prototype and compatibility fixture for repository and accepted-artifact requirements.
Exercise required/optional, budget exhaustion, stale currentness and authority-negative cases before narrowing worker scope.

researchGaps: Select exact ContextRequirement and ContextResolution fields and canonical identity/hash inputs.
Define required versus optional evidence and the semantics of a partial resolution under a hard context budget.
Map current Backend/QA source shapes into compatibility fixtures without preserving application-specific final ports.
Decide whether a small contracts package is needed or the semantic contract belongs entirely under packages/oracle.
Obtain a new Jev readiness judgment after contract experiments close all gaps.
negativeVerificationCases: A caller embeds provider/tool commands in ContextRequirement or bypasses the semantic resolution seam.
A stale or provenance-incomplete required context item is represented as current.
Oracle/provider/planner code attempts to claim work, accept product output, publish product truth or own domain recovery.

supersededAuthority.rule: Historical readiness/Jev artifacts remain evidence only; changed objective/plan bindings make them non-authoritative for execution.
